sn35.140:1.2: The cause and condition for the arising of the eye is also impermanent.
sn35.140:1.3: As the eye has originated from what is impermanent, how could it be permanent?
sn35.140:1.8: The cause and condition for the arising of the mind is also impermanent.
sn35.140:1.9: As the mind has originated from what is impermanent, how could it be permanent?
sn35.140:1.10: “Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple experiences revulsion towards the eye … towards the mind.
sn35.140:1.11: Experiencing revulsion, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion his mind is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated.’
sn35.140:1.12: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”
